record.title: Gorenstein conjecture for directed tree Gaussian models
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a directed tree, let $I_T$ be the toric ideal associated with its Gaussian tree model, and let $\mathbb{C}[\Sigma]/I_T$ be the corresponding quotient ring.

**Gorenstein tree conjecture.** The quotient ring $\mathbb{C}[\Sigma]/I_T$ is Gorenstein if and only if every vertex of $T$ has degree at most three.

The ring is known to be normal and Cohen–Macaulay for every tree, so the conjecture concerns the sharper Gorenstein property. The paper leaves this characterization open.
record.source_name: Seth Sullivant, “Algebraic geometry of Gaussian Bayesian networks”, arXiv:0704.0918 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0918

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2007).

record.title: The constraining conjecture for minimal three-edge-connected simple graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a minimal three edge connected simple graph. A twisted graph has the form $T=(\vec{G},G,<,A)$, where $\vec{G}$ is a directed graph on $G$, $<$ is a total order, and $A$ is the associated constraint set; it is constraining when the corresponding strict system is insoluble while the associated homogeneous system has a nontrivial solution.

**Constraining conjecture.** For every minimal three edge connected simple graph $G$, there is a directed graph $\vec{G}$, a total order $<$, and a constraining twisted graph $T=(\vec{G},G,<,A)$.

This is stated as a still weaker consequence of the preceding conjectures. It would provide a graph-theoretic route to the required obstruction and line-arrangement constructions, but is unresolved in the source.
record.source_name: Jeremy J. Carroll, “A New Proof of Pappus's Theorem”, arXiv:0704.3424 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.3424

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2007). “This conjecture was disproved first by using oriented matroid techniques over a 32 point dual construction.”

record.title: Naserasr's planar graph power conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal{P}_{2k+1}$ be the class of planar graphs with odd-girth at least $2k+1$. For a graph $G$, write $G^{(2k-1)}$ for its $(2k-1)$st power and $\chi$ for chromatic number. **Naserasr's conjecture.** For every $G\in\mathcal{P}_{2k+1}$,

$$
\chi(G^{(2k-1)})\leq 2^{2k}.
$$

The source presents this as an upper-bound conjecture for powers of planar graphs and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Hossein Hajiabolhassan, “On Colorings of Graph Powers”, arXiv:0708.0704 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.0704

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2007). “This conjecture however was proved by Tardif recently (personal communication, see ).”

record.title: The infinitude of primes of every odd weight at least 3
record.statement: Let $p_n$ denote the $n$th prime, and let its weight be the weight in the paper's decomposition of primes. **Odd-weight prime conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge 3$ that is not a multiple of $2$, the number of primes with weight equal to $k$ is infinite. The claim extends the weight-three formulation of the twin prime conjecture by analogy with the corresponding result for natural numbers; no rigorous argument is given.
record.source_name: Remi Eismann, “Decomposition into weight * level + jump and application to a new classification of primes”, arXiv:0711.0865 (2010).

record.title: Property B for zero-sum free subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_n^2$
record.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. A subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n^2$ is **zero-sum free** if no nonempty subset of $A$ has sum equal to $0$ in $\mathbb{Z}_n^2$. We say that $n$ satisfies property $B$ if every zero-sum free subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n^2$ contains an element whose multiplicity is at least $n-2$. **Property B conjecture.** Every integer $n$ satisfies property $B$. This is presented as a plausible conjecture concerning the structure of maximal zero-sum free sets; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

record.title: Woodall's modified positivity conjecture for bipartite planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite planar graph, and let $P_G(q)$ denote its chromatic polynomial. Define

$$
B_5=\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}.
$$

**Woodall's modified conjecture.**

$$
P_G(q)>0
$$

for every real $q\geq B_5$.

The paper notes that this modifies Woodall's conjecture, which fails for $k=2$, and is motivated by numerical roots approaching $B_5$ from below. Its status is left open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Jesus Salas and Alan D. Sokal, “Transfer Matrices and Partition-Function Zeros for Antiferromagnetic Potts Models. V. Further Results for the Square-Lattice Chromatic Polynomial”, arXiv:0711.1738 (2009).

record.title: Positivity conjecture for plane quadrangulations above three
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane quadrangulation, meaning a plane graph whose faces are bounded by four edges, and let $P_G(q)$ denote its chromatic polynomial. **The quadrangulation positivity conjecture.**

$$
P_G(q)>0
$$

for every real $q\geq 3$.

The paper motivates this weakened conjecture using the height representation of the square-lattice zero-temperature 3-state Potts antiferromagnet and states no resolution in the supplied text.

record.title: Adamus's degree-sum conjecture for long cycles
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, undirected graph with no loops or multiple edges. Write $d(v)$ for the degree of a vertex $v$. Suppose that $G$ is $2$-connected, has order $n\geq3$ with $n\neq5,7$, and let $k<n/2$ be an integer. **Adamus's degree-sum conjecture.** If

$$
d(x)+d(y)\geq n-k
$$

for every pair of non-adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$, then $G$ contains a cycle of length $n-k$, unless $G$ is bipartite and $n-k\equiv1\pmod{2}$. This generalizes Ore's degree-sum condition for Hamiltonicity to long cycles; the conjecture is known to hold when $k=1$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Janusz Adamus, “A note on a degree sum condition for long cycles in graphs”, arXiv:0711.4394 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.4394

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2007).

record.title: Partition conjecture relating characteristic posets and regularity
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and let $J\subset I$ be monomial ideals. Let $P_{I/J}$ be the characteristic poset of $I/J$, and let $\operatorname{reg}(I/J)$ denote the regularity of the graded $S$-module $I/J$. For $c,d\in P_{I/J}$, write $[c,d]$ for the interval between them, and for $c=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ write $|c|=c_1+\cdots+c_n$. **Partition conjecture.** There exists a partition

$$
\mathcal P: P_{I/J}=\bigcup_{i=1}^r[c_i,d_i]
$$

of $P_{I/J}$ such that $|c_i|\leq\operatorname{reg}(I/J)$ for all $i$. The conjecture is presented as following from a conjecture of Soleyman Jahan; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Jürgen Herzog, Marius Vladoiu and Xinxian Zheng, “How to compute the Stanley depth of a monomial ideal”, arXiv:0712.2308 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.2308

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2007).

record.title: Zhang's metric-graph lower-bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $g\geq2$ be an integer. A **pm-graph** $\overline{\Gamma}$ of genus $g$ is a polarized metric graph of genus $g$. Let $\varphi(\overline{\Gamma})$ be its Zhang-type invariant, and let $\ell_0(\overline{\Gamma})$ and $\ell_i(\overline{\Gamma})$ denote the total lengths of the edges of types $0$ and $i$, respectively.

**Zhang's conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $c(g)$ such that for every pm-graph $\overline{\Gamma}$ of genus $g$,

$$
\varphi(\overline{\Gamma})\geq c(g)\ell_0(\overline{\Gamma})+\sum_{i\in(0,g/2]}\frac{2i(g-i)}{g}\ell_i(\overline{\Gamma}).
$$

The paper proves this inequality for genera $2$, $3$, and $4$, with explicit constants, and formulates it in general as a conjectural graph-theoretic lower bound underlying the geometric Bogomolov conjecture.
record.source_name: X. W. C. Faber, “The Geometric Bogomolov Conjecture for Small Genus Curves”, arXiv:0803.0855 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.0855

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2008).

record.title: The planarity characterization by torsion conjecture for graph braid groups
record.statement: For a graph $\Gamma$ and an integer $n\geq 2$, let $B_n\Gamma$ be its graph braid group and let $H_1(B_n\Gamma)$ be its first homology group. **Planarity–torsion conjecture.** For every $n\geq 2$, the graph $\Gamma$ is planar if and only if $H_1(B_n\Gamma)$ is torsion-free. The non-planar implication is established in the source via $2$-torsion in first homology; the converse is proposed based on the preceding conjecture.
record.source_name: Jee Hyoun Kim, Ki Hyoung Ko and Hyo Won Park, “Graph braid groups and right-angled Artin groups”, arXiv:0805.0082 (2010).
record.references:

record.title: t-unimodality of refined Eulerian polynomials by cycle type
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition of $n$ with exactly $k$ parts of size $1$. The polynomial $A_{\lambda}^{{\rm maj},{\rm des},{\rm exc}}(q,p,q^{-1}t)$ is $t$-symmetric with center of symmetry $(n-k)/2$.

**Cycle-type t-unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial $A_{\lambda}^{{\rm maj},{\rm des},{\rm exc}}(q,p,q^{-1}t)$ is $t$-unimodal with center of symmetry $(n-k)/2$. Consequently, for all $n,k$, $A_{n,k}^{{\rm maj},{\rm des},{\rm exc}}(q,p,q^{-1}t)$ is $t$-symmetric and $t$-unimodal with center of symmetry $(n-k)/2$.

The symmetry is proved immediately before the conjecture; the conjectural part is the corresponding unimodality, which would give a cycle-type refinement of the earlier fixed-point results.
record.source_name: John Shareshian and Michelle L. Wachs, “Eulerian quasisymmetric functions and poset topology”, arXiv:0805.2416 (2008).

record.title: Crystallographic q-specialization conjecture for q,t-Fuss-Catalan numbers
record.statement:
Let $W$ be a crystallographic reflection group, and let $\operatorname{Cat}^{(m)}(W,q)$ be the combinatorial $q$-Fuss-Catalan number obtained by summing $q^{\operatorname{coh}(R)}$ over the positive regions $R$ of the extended Shi arrangement. **Crystallographic q-specialization conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Cat}^{(m)}(W,q,1)=\operatorname{Cat}^{(m)}(W,q).
$$

The conjecture would partially answer the paper's open problem concerning combinatorial statistics realizing the two-parameter polynomial. The type $A$ result for all $m$ and the type $B$ result for $m=1$ are established in the supplied context, but the stated general crystallographic claim remains unresolved there.
record.source_name: Christian Stump, “q,t-Fuss-Catalan numbers for complex reflection groups”, arXiv:0806.2936 (2008).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2008).

record.title: Dobbertin's conjecture on APN permutations in even dimension
record.statement:
Let $m\geq 1$ be a natural number, let $A=({\mathbb F}_2)^m$, and let an **APN function** be a vectorial Boolean function $F:A\to A$ with differential uniformity $2$, meaning that

$$
\delta_F(a,b)=\left|\{x\in A:F(x+a)+F(x)=b\}\right|\leq 2
$$

for every $a\in A\setminus\{0\}$ and $b\in A$. **Dobbertin's conjecture.** If $m$ is even, no APN function $F:A\to A$ is a permutation of $A$. This conjecture concerns the existence of cryptographically optimal vectorial Boolean functions: APN functions have the lowest possible differential uniformity, while the nonexistence of APN permutations in even dimension remains an open problem in general.
record.source_name: A. Caranti, F. Dalla Volta and M. Sala, “On some block ciphers and imprimitive groups”, arXiv:0806.4135 (2008).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

record.title: Nash-Williams' weak Hamilton degree-sequence conjecture for digraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a digraph on $n\geq 3$ vertices, with nondecreasing outdegree and indegree sequences $d^+_1\leq\dots\leq d^+_n$ and $d^-_1\leq\dots\leq d^-_n$. **Nash-Williams' conjecture.** If $d^+_i,d^-_i\geq i+1$ for all $i<(n-1)/2$, and, when $n$ is odd,

$$
d^+_{\lceil n/2\rceil},d^-_{\lceil n/2\rceil}\geq\lceil n/2\rceil,
$$

then $G$ contains a Hamilton cycle. This is a weakening of the strongly connected degree-sequence conjecture and would give a digraph analogue of Pósa's theorem.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn, Deryk Osthus and Andrew Treglown, “Hamiltonian degree sequences in digraphs”, arXiv:0807.1827 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.1827

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2008). “It is even an open problem whether the conditions imply the existence of a cycle through any pair of given vertices (see ).”

record.title: Strong deformation retraction for moduli spaces of metric graphs of arbitrary genus
record.statement: Let $MG_{g,n}^{\mathfrak{v}}$ be the moduli space of metric graphs of genus $g$ with $n$ marked points on vertices, and let $TM_{g,n}$ be the corresponding tropical moduli space. **Strong deformation retraction conjecture.** The space $TM_{g,n}$ is the strong deformation retract of $MG_{g,n}^{\mathfrak{v}}$ for all $g\geq 0$ and $n\geq 0$. This is presented as a more speculative extension of the genus-$1$ claim; the preceding argument establishes only an ordinary deformation retraction in genus $1$, so the arbitrary-genus assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Dmitry N. Kozlov, “Moduli spaces of metric graphs of genus 1 with marks on vertices”, arXiv:0809.4364 (2008).

record.title: Alev's completeness conjecture for the constructed B_n graph solutions
record.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the type-$B_n$ case, and consider the equation referred to in the source as Equation. Starting from the simple graphs and applying the construction described immediately before the conjecture, one obtains $\pi(n)$ graphs, where $\pi(n)$ denotes the number of partitions of $n$.

**Alev's completeness conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 2$, these $\pi(n)$ constructed graphs are the only solutions of the equation.

The claim would classify all solutions in the $B_n$ case by the preceding graph construction. No general proof or disproof is supplied in the source.

record.title: Bounded-representation subsequence conjecture for the binary Goldbach-type problem
record.statement:
Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be arbitrary positive numbers, and let $T$ be a subsequence of the primes. **Bounded-representation conjecture.** There is no such $T$ for which every odd integer $m\geq C_1$ has between $1$ and $C_2$ distinct representations of the form

$$
m=p+2q,
$$

where $p,q\in T$.
This conjecture is posed in connection with the preceding unique-representation question and concerns whether a prime subsequence can provide uniformly bounded positive representation counts; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Vladimir Shevelev, “On Unique Additive Representations of Positive Integers and Some Close Problems”, arXiv:0811.0290 (2008).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2008).

record.title: Ziegler's conjecture for r-stable Kneser hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $KG^r(n,k)$ be the Kneser hypergraph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of $[n]$, and call a subset $S\subseteq[n]$ **$r$-stable** when any two elements $x,y\in S$ satisfy $r\leq |x-y|\leq n-r$. Let $KG^r(n,k)_{r\text{-}\mathrm{Stab}}$ be the sub-hypergraph induced by the $r$-stable vertices. **Ziegler's conjecture.** For all $n\geq rk$ and $r\geq2$, its chromatic number is

$$
\chi\bigl(KG^r(n,k)_{r\text{-}\mathrm{Stab}}\bigr)=\left\lceil\frac{n-r(k-1)}{r-1}\right\rceil.
$$

This asserts that the Alon–Frankl–Lovász chromatic-number formula remains valid after restricting to $r$-stable vertices. The source attributes the conjecture to Ziegler; no resolution status is supplied here.
